$comment: Gemfall beat 7, the Tether's chapter 7 (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 7L). Three instruments are chapter props (tether_ledger, tether_chord, tether_question); honest ways to them are checks, double games are certain but cost a friend's trust (wardens_trust is set false when the party sells the wardens' secrets to the choir) or a stone. Every ending sets climbed_the_mountain. The seal clock is set once per path: scene_tether_holds (clock_steady), scene_tether_slips (clock_late), or ending_lost_in_echoes (clock_late, the lost-fight setback). facet_caravan is defined in gemfall-07h. Pacing episodes on the spine (the table's rule vote, the two scouts, the first sitting, the returning cart, the night visitor, the rope bridge, the crowds at the bend, who keeps the table) set only chapter-local flags; practiced, two_helpers and table_works open extra TN 12 ways into the test.
title: The Tether

plate.narration: A table made from a door waits between two barrels. A warden stands on one side, a bark-mask singer on the other. A dragonling grandmother keeps knitting. Somehow, this road needs everyone to listen at the same table.

objectives.label: Held the Caravan Stone's hum still for one whole breath
Kept the wardens' trust to the very end

goal.text: Gather the ledger, the chord and a true answer, then hold the stone's hum at the bend.

steps.label: Face the stone's hum at the bend

tether_ledger.name: The Cage-Doctrine Ledger
tether_ledger.text: The wardens' plan for holding what is under the mountain. They do not lend it.

tether_chord.name: The Resonance Chord
tether_chord.text: Three notes the choir hums to make the stones hum back. Written down nowhere.

tether_question.name: The Witch's Question
tether_question.text: What do you actually want? A witch lent it to you. You may ask it of anything.

scene_the_table.narration: Pellam the clerk walks you down to the Pinch, a gap between two red hills. "You said hold it," he says. "Not break it. So: gather the ledger, the chord and a true answer, then hold the stone's hum at the bend." The stone rides in tomorrow's caravan, so loud the mules wear earmuffs. The chord belongs to Hessa's friends, the Deep Hollow, who sing in bark masks.

scene_the_table_grandmothers_chair.narration: A grandmother brings her knitting and a stool, and says nothing at all. Soon a warden and a mask stop shouting. It is very hard to shout near a knitting grandmother. "Well?" she says. "Build it."

choice_the_rule.narration: Your door-table stands between the wardens and the masked choir. Chalk one rule on it. Quiet voices make room for questions. Faces showing help people work together. Sharing gives them something to pass across.

choice_the_rule_no_shouting.narration: You chalk NOBODY SHOUTS across the door. Five minutes later, a warden forgets and shouts. Everybody looks at the chalk. He goes red and pours tea for everyone, which turns out to be the punishment.

choice_the_rule_masks_up.narration: You chalk MASKS UP, FACES SHOWING. A young mask pushes hers up, and she has freckles. The warden across from her blinks, as if he forgot there were people under there. Soon the others do it too.

choice_the_rule_bring_one.narration: You chalk BRING ONE THING TO SHARE. By noon the table holds a cookie tin, a pot of soup, some honeycomb, and an old map nobody can read. People sit down just to see.

scene_ledger.narration: At the wardens' camp, Pellam sits behind a desk. The wardens' ledger holds all their rules and plans. It is as thick as a doorstep and chained to the desk. "It never leaves this desk," he says. Then he looks at the desk, as if he said something more useful than he meant.

scene_ledger_false_promise.narration: You promise him the choir's secret chord. You do not mean it. Pellam writes the promise down and makes you watch. The ledger feels heavy all the way up the valley, and not because of the pages.

scene_ledger_friend.narration: "We're asking as friends," you say. Pellam looks at the chain a long time. Then he unlocks it and writes LENT in a column never used before. "Bring it back. I shall know if a page is bent."

check_ledger.prompt: Work out how to carry a chained ledger and its desk up the valley together

onSuccess.narration: Two poles, a rope and a lot of squinting. You turn the desk into a little throne on poles, with the ledger riding on top, still chained, and off it goes up the valley, desk and all. Pellam reads his own rule twice, frowns at it twice, and cannot find a single word wrong. Nobody has ever seen Pellam almost smile. He very nearly does.

onFailure.narration: You try poles. You try rope. You try lifting the whole desk at once, and the chain goes clank, and the desk does not go anywhere. Pellam writes NOT LENT in his column, very neatly. You leave with nothing but a very clear picture of the cover.

scene_two_scouts.narration: Up the valley, two young people play tug-of-war with a choir sash. A warden cadet called Linnet pulls one end. A young mask called Rook pulls the other. "Tell her it's ours!" puffs Rook. "Tell him it's evidence!" puffs Linnet. They both want you to decide.

check_two_scouts.prompt: Hold the middle of a tug-of-war so neither side wins

onSuccess.narration: You take the middle of the rope and dig in your heels. Linnet pulls. Rook pulls. You hold, right in the middle, and nobody moves an inch. At last they both let go at once and sit down hard in the heather, laughing. Linnet holds out her hand. Rook looks at it as if it might bite, then shakes it.

onFailure.narration: You grab the middle, but the sash slides through your hands, and both of them land in the heather. They stomp off to tell their bosses. But they stomp off the same way, and the last you see of them, they are arguing in a way that sounds a lot like talking.

scene_two_scouts_fib.narration: You tell each of them what they want to hear. Both go off happy. Later you see them on one rock, comparing notes. They both look up at you at exactly the same moment.

scene_two_scouts_table_stone.narration: You set down the Table Stone from the truth-table at Redspire. It hums. Linnet knows it from the citadel. Rook knows the note from the choir. They drop the rope to listen. "It's the same stone," they say together.

scene_choir.narration: Up the valley, Hessa's soup-tent people, the Deep Hollow, hum in a ring with their bark masks pushed up. "We wake the mountain gently, so it can fix things," Hessa whispers. Their chord is three notes long, and they never teach it to strangers.

variants.text: Your {facets} great stones hum loudest of all. The singers glance at each other.

scene_choir_hum_along.narration: Your kitsune hums along, badly, then not badly at all. Soon the choir forgets your kitsune is not one of them, and sings the whole chord out plain.

scene_choir_pay_stone.narration: You pay with a rush gem. The choir passes it around, humming, and then it is gone into a sack. They teach you the chord. Your pack feels one gem lighter.

scene_choir_sell_secrets.narration: You trade them the wardens' plans, page by page. "Pellam will know," says Hessa, not unkindly, and teaches you the chord. The ledger feels lighter, and that is not a good feeling.

scene_choir_vouch.narration: The grandmother hums with them, a low knitting sort of hum. The choir softens, the way a room does when a grandma walks in. "Teach them," she says. And they do.

check_chord.prompt: Hum three notes back to a whole masked choir, true and steady

onSuccess.narration: Hessa hums the first note. You hum it back. She hums the second. You hum it back, wobbly. The third is so low it buzzes in your teeth, and you hold it anyway. The whole choir goes quiet. "Don't make me sorry," says Hessa.

onFailure.narration: They sing it for you once, very fast, and then pull their masks down. You match the first note. Only the first.

scene_first_sitting.narration: Back at the table, Pellam sits on one side and Hessa on the other. Nobody speaks. Then the ground shrugs. The folded sock under the short leg shoots out, and the table tips. Hessa grabs her soup. Pellam grabs his ledger. Everyone looks at you.

check_first_sitting.prompt: Fix a wobbly table while two sides watch you do it

onSuccess.narration: A flat stone, a bit of string and a lot of squinting. The table stands dead level. Pellam tests it with his pencil, which does not roll. Hessa tests it with her soup, which does not spill. They both nod, at the table, which is nearly the same as nodding at each other.

onFailure.narration: You fix it. Now it wobbles toward Hessa instead. You fix it again. Now it wobbles both ways at once. Pellam makes a small noise that might be a laugh, and Hessa definitely laughs, and somehow, after that, they both stay sitting down.

scene_first_sitting_wobbly_side.narration: You swap seats and hold the wobbly side level with your elbows. It is not comfortable. Pellam and Hessa both notice, and both lean in a little.

variants.text: You swap seats and hold the wobbly side level with your elbows. It is not comfortable. Pellam and Hessa both notice, and both lean in a little.

scene_first_sitting_grandmother.narration: The grandmother rests one foot under the short corner without dropping a stitch, and leaves it there all afternoon. Nobody dares tip the table after that.

scene_road_gifts.narration: Pellam reads from his notebook. "Hold it. That is what you told me at the citadel. Still your word?" It is. Then the road starts bringing back things you did on the way here, as if the realm kept your receipts.

scene_ossley.narration: A frog in a very old hat poles a flat boat up a dry creek: Old Ossley, the frog from the reeds of the Great River. He looks at your packs. "Leashes are for things that want to run," he says. Then nothing for quite a while.

scene_ossley_debt.narration: Ossley's price was never coin. "Whatever you tie," he says, "tie it with a knot you can undo." He makes you show him, right there, on his boat rope. It takes three tries.

scene_mosshome_runner.narration: A MossHome runner jogs up with mules, carrying things the Woods took from careless hunters. Your knotted cord says some are yours. She unloads it all with a message: "Whatever you are tying, tie it loose."

scene_boggart.narration: A boggart with a satchel of scribbled paper sidles up, not looking at you. "Catalog," it tells nobody. "Who bought what. Who sold to who. Costs one really good sentence you overheard."

scene_boggart_choir_said.narration: You hum what the choir hums when nobody is listening: the same three notes, only sadder. The boggart goes completely still. "Sidelong," it says at last, approvingly, and hands over the catalog without looking at you.

scene_boggart_brisk_said.narration: You repeat what Pellam mutters to his ledger, which is mostly numbers and one quiet "oh dear." The boggart hugs itself. "A clerk's oh dear," it tells nobody. "Rarer than rubies." It hands over the catalog.

scene_ford_witch.narration: Mother Thrum, the witch from the ford, has come up the road with a ringing wool sock. "I always ask twice," she says. "Answer true, and I'll lend you my question. What do you actually want?"

scene_ford_witch_flatter.narration: You say whatever might get you the question. "No," says Mother Thrum pleasantly. "That's not a want. That's a wish for a want." Her charms ring once, amused.

scene_ford_witch_hold_power.narration: Mother Thrum does not look away. "Honest. I'll give you honest." She lends you the question, but holds it a heartbeat longer than she needs to. "Ask it of yourselves first."

scene_ford_witch_hold_safe.narration: Mother Thrum nods once. "That one I'll lend." She presses the question into your hands like a small warm coin. "Ask it of anything. Even me." Then she tips a stone from the ford out of her sock.

scene_stall_witch.narration: At the end of the road, a witch in a patched hat runs a remedy stall. Every charm on it rings by itself. "Answer my question first," she says, "and I'll lend it to you. What do you actually want?"

scene_stall_witch_flatter.narration: You say whatever might get you the question. "No," says the stall witch pleasantly. "That's not a want. That's a wish for a want." Her charms ring once, amused.

scene_stall_witch_hold_power.narration: The stall witch does not look away. "Honest. I'll give you honest." She lends you the question, but holds it a heartbeat longer than she needs to. "Ask it of yourselves first."

scene_stall_witch_hold_safe.narration: The stall witch nods once. "That one I'll lend," she says, and presses the question into your hands like a small warm coin. "Ask it of anything. Even me."

scene_returning_cart.narration: On the way back, a grandmother's cart of stones going home is stuck on the steep bit. "Only a little stuck, dear," she puffs. But tomorrow is the test, and you have never held a hum still. One afternoon left. Help, or practice?

check_returning_cart.prompt: Push a cart full of stones up the steep bit

onSuccess.narration: Shoulders down, everybody push. The cart groans up the steep bit and over the top. The grandmother hands a warm bead from her apron to every hand, and says, "Practice tonight, dears. You'll need it."

onFailure.narration: The cart rolls back two steps for every three you push it. In the end you sit on the back of it like a seesaw while the grandmother pulls, and between you it gets over the top. She laughs so hard she has to sit down.

scene_returning_cart_practice.narration: You leave the cart to a passing warden and find a quiet rock. You hold a small humming stone between your hands and try to make it still. It takes all afternoon. Then, for half a breath, it stops. You feel it at once, like a held door. Behind you, the cart gets up the hill without you.

scene_returning_cart_both.narration: Your bigfoot pushes the cart one-handed, like a stroller, holding a humming stone in the other hand. Halfway up, the stone goes still for half a breath. The grandmother has never seen anything like it.

scene_evening.narration: Evening. The wardens' fires and the masks' fires are as far apart as they can get. Your table sits right in the middle. Somebody has left a cup of tea on it.

scene_evening_between.narration: You walk the dark road between the camps. One side sings a counting song. The other sings the same tune with different words. Neither knows. In the middle, it sounds like one song.

scene_centaur_relay.narration: A centaur relay pulls up and unrolls a sash-map. "Fat caravan tomorrow," says the lead runner. "Where do you want it?" You point at the worst bend. She nods, as if that is the most sensible thing all day.

scene_relay_sing.narration: The centaur relay singers at the campfires sing about wagons that have not come yet. A grandmother's runner brings you a list of caves nobody may ever dig. It is exactly the list a seal's keeper would keep.

scene_ember.narration: "Darlings!" cries Madame Coralie Fenn from her barrel on wheels, tied to a caravan roof. She has the warm red stone you sold her on the quay, your very first. It sits in a velvet box, and its price has gone way up.

scene_ember_wave.narration: You wave. Madame Fenn waves back with both arms, and her barrel wobbles. "Next time, darlings!" The caravan rolls on, with your very first stone humming on top.

scene_ember_buy_back.narration: You pay. Madame Fenn hugs the velvet box before handing it over. "I always hoped it would be you, darlings." The Ember Facet is warm as toast, and it hums as if it remembers you.

scene_night_visitor.narration: Late at night, Pellam comes to your table alone. "One question," he says quietly. "Where does the choir sing at night? I only want to know." Across the road, by a mask's fire, somebody goes very still.

scene_night_visitor_tell.narration: You tell him. Pellam writes it down twice and thanks you. Across the road, the still mask gets up and goes into a tent. Nobody mentions it in the morning. Nobody has to.

scene_night_visitor_not_mine.narration: "That isn't ours to tell," you say. Pellam nods and writes one word in his notebook: FAIR. He underlines it twice and goes back to bed.

check_night_visitor.prompt: Get a warden clerk and a choir singer to ask each other their own questions

onSuccess.narration: Hessa comes over with two cups of soup. Pellam takes one. They talk until the fire is embers, about the mountain, and the rules, and which of them is more tired. When they go back to their own sides, they say goodnight to each other. Out loud.

onFailure.narration: Hessa comes over, but she and Pellam sit at opposite ends and only talk to you. "Ask him why," says Hessa. "Ask her what for," says Pellam. You pass the questions back and forth until midnight. It is slow. It is still talking.

rest_under_the_table.narration: You sleep under your table, between the two camps. In the night, a warden and a mask both come to borrow the teapot. They stand there, not looking at each other, until somebody says please. Patch up your scrapes.

scene_rope_bridge.narration: The road crosses a deep gully on a rope bridge. Each time the ground shrugs, it swings like a hammock with opinions. A snowhorn goat stands in the middle, chewing, refusing to move.

check_rope_bridge.prompt: Everyone dash across a swinging bridge between tremors

onSuccess.narration: You wait for the swing to settle, then go, light as leaves. The goat watches you squeeze past it, chews thoughtfully, and follows you off the far end, as if that had been its plan all along.

onFailure.narration: Halfway over, the ground shrugs and the bridge swings, and you end up clinging to the goat, who does not mind at all. When it stops swinging, the goat walks you the rest of the way across, very slowly, like a nanny.

scene_rope_bridge_roped.narration: You rope yourselves together and go over so slowly a snail would be embarrassed. When the bridge swings, you all lean the same way at once. The goat lets you pass.

variants.text: You tie yourself to the handrail and go over so slowly a snail would be embarrassed. When the bridge swings, you lean with it. The goat lets you pass.

scene_rope_bridge_loose_knot.narration: You tie on to the handrail with a loose knot. Every few steps you untie it and tie it farther along. It is slow and very safe. By the far side, you could tie that knot in your sleep.

scene_switchback.narration: Halfway up, the road runs through a narrow cutting. An echo hunter hides in the rock, repeating every sound you make, half a breath late. With it comes a lone cinder wolf, ears flat.

scene_switchback_fly_over.narration: You fly over the cutting. The echo hunter copies the sound of your wings and gets very confused. The wolf is already gone.

scene_switchback_sprite_knots.narration: Tiny grass knots, tied at ankle height, lead up and over the cutting. The harvest sprites are still looking out for you. Below, the echo repeats your footsteps to an empty road.

check_echoes.prompt: Make the cutting so noisy the echo cannot pick one sound to follow

onSuccess.narration: Clapping, stamping, humming, one terrible whistle. The echo hunter cannot choose, gets a headache, and backs off into the rocks. The wolf, who hates the noise even more, runs straight past you.

onFailure.narration: Somebody stops a moment too early, and in the silence the echo hunter hears exactly one heartbeat. Yours.

encounter_echoes.narration: The echo hunter unfolds out of the rock wall. The wolf, scared half silly, sticks close beside it.

onVictory.narration: The echo hunter folds back into the rock, sulking. The wolf bolts downhill.

onDefeat.narration: The echoes get so loud you cannot think. You stumble back down the switchback, stones rattling.

scene_bend_crowds.narration: At the worst bend, wardens stack numbered boxes on one side. Masks unroll sacks on the other. Both plan to grab the big stone the moment it arrives, which would end your test before it starts. Far below, the caravan is coming.

scene_bend_crowds_chalk_line.narration: You draw a chalk line across the road and stand on it. "Give us one breath to try," you say. "Then you can argue." Nobody wants to cross first, so nobody does.

check_bend_crowds.prompt: Talk both sides into lending you one helper each

onSuccess.narration: A warden steps over, and then, after a long pause, a mask. They stand on either side of you, not looking at each other, ready to help. It is the first time all season they have stood on the same bit of road.

onFailure.narration: Both sides send their grumpiest. The two of them argue about where to stand until the caravan is nearly here. But while they are arguing, nobody else grabs anything, which is almost as good.

scene_bend_crowds_scouts.narration: Linnet and Rook run from opposite ends of the bend and stand beside you. Both sides stare. Then they put down their boxes and sacks. You cannot grab something from under your own people.

choice_the_test.narration: The fattest caravan is coming. The stone in its middle wagon hums so loudly the mules wear earmuffs. This is Pellam's test: hold that hum still for one breath, like a hand on a ringing bell. Wardens on one side, masks on the other, all watching you.

variants.text: You have only rush gems. But both camps have small tuning stones on their tables, and nobody would mind if you borrowed some.
Your great stones lean toward the wagon, like iron filings toward a magnet.
All {facets} great stones lean toward the wagon at once.

choice_the_test_borrowed.narration: A warden hands you a gray tuning stone. A mask hands you a red one. Neither looks at the other. You let them hum together until they find one note. Now you have an instrument, borrowed from both sides.

check_hold_easy.prompt: Ask the stone in the wagon what it actually wants, and listen for the answer

onSuccess.narration: You ask the witch's question out loud. The stone goes quiet, the way a person goes quiet when somebody finally asks the right thing. For one long breath, nothing on the whole hillside hums at all.

onFailure.narration: You ask the question, but the ground lurches halfway through and the stone never hears the end of it. The hum leaps free, and the whole hillside answers it.

check_hold.prompt: Lay your hands on the wagon stone and hold its hum still for one whole breath

onSuccess.narration: For one long breath the humming stops, like a bell under a hand. The mules take their earmuffs off. The wardens stop writing. The masks stop humming. Then it starts again, softer, as if it is listening to you. It feels like holding a leash, loose and steady.

onFailure.narration: You almost have it. Then the hum slides through your fingers like a fish, and the whole hillside answers it.

check_hold_hard.prompt: Put your bare hands on the wagon stone and hold its hum still, with nothing else to help

onSuccess.narration: No ledger, no chord, no question. Just you, holding on. And for one long breath, astonishingly, it is enough.

onFailure.narration: It is like trying to hold a thunderstorm in a teacup. The hum leaps free, and the whole hillside answers it.

scene_tether_holds.narration: The caravan master climbs down and hands you the Caravan Stone. "Please keep it. It's been humming at me for a month." A mask takes off her mask. For a moment, everyone is looking at you.

variants.text: It is your only great stone, and it hums like a small, loud heart.
Your other great stones hum back at it like old friends.
That makes {facets} great stones, humming like a choir.

scene_tether_slips.narration: The hum jumps free, and the ground answers with a long, rolling shake. In the muddle, the masks drive the wagon up a side track, saying sorry. The tremors settle into a slow, patient rhythm.

scene_who_keeps_table.narration: Before you climb, you go back to the Pinch. Your old door still sits on its barrels, chalk and all. People are packing up and running. "Somebody must keep the table while you're up the mountain," says Pellam, "or there will be nothing to come back to." Who?

variants.text: It may be the greatest thing you have made.
Your great stones hum faintly, as if they want to stay and watch.
Your {facets} great stones hum, like a realm trying to stay in one piece.

check_who_keeps_table.prompt: Get Pellam and Hessa to pick up the old door together

onSuccess.narration: Pellam looks at Hessa. Hessa looks at Pellam. Then they each take one end of the old door and lift it together. "Mind the short leg," says Hessa. "I've logged the short leg," says Pellam. They carry it down the hill side by side.

onFailure.narration: They cannot agree whose end is the front. In the end they carry it down the hill sideways, both talking at once. But they carry it together, and they do not put it down.

scene_who_keeps_table_grandmother.narration: Two grandmothers tuck the table under their arms like a tray and carry it downhill, still knitting. "We'll keep your chalk on it, dear. Somebody will want reminding."

scene_who_keeps_table_ossley.narration: Old Ossley, the frog from the reeds of the Great River, poles his flat boat up the dry creek as if he had been waiting. He lays your table across his boat like a roof. "Tables float," he says. That is all.

rest_up_the_mountain.narration: At the tree line you look back. Wardens, masks and mules are running downhill, together for once. You turn and climb the mountain everyone else is leaving. You said hold it. Now you find out.

variants.text: You have only rush gems, and the tune. The tune will have to do.
{facets} great stones climb with you. The mountain can hear you coming.

ending_lost_in_echoes.narration: By the time the echoes let you go, the caravan is long gone, and the ground shakes in a slow, patient rhythm. Nobody is at the table. You climb anyway, far behind, humming to keep your courage up.

interaction_set_table.narration: In the middle of the Pinch lie an old door and two barrels of different heights. "A table," says Pellam, tapping it with his pencil. "Level, please. I will be measuring."

interaction.cue: Everyone lift or lower your side until the door is flat, then carry it onto the barrels.

onSuccess.narration: The door settles, almost flat. Pellam's pencil rolls only a little. "Acceptable," he says, which from Pellam is a cheer.

onFailure.narration: The door slides off with a thump. "Almost level," says Pellam kindly. "Nobody will notice." Everybody notices.

onAssisted.narration: Pellam props one corner with his boot. The door settles onto the barrels, almost flat. "Acceptable," he says.

interaction_choir_warmup.narration: Before you leave, Hessa taps her mask. "Warm-up," she says. "I hum, you hum back. No giggling at the low one."

interaction.cue: Watch the notes glow, then hum them back in order.

onSuccess.narration: The last note hangs in the air. A singer ties a ribbon to your pack. "For luck. Don't tell the others I'm soft."

onFailure.narration: You lose the third note. The choir hums the rest for you, gently. Somebody's mask slips off, giggling.

onAssisted.narration: The choir hums under you until the last note comes out right. A singer ties a ribbon to your pack. "For luck," she whispers.

interaction_tea_cups.narration: You carry the tea across with helpers from both camps. A warden turns his cup to hide the words NOT SOUP. Not a drop spills. Hessa sends back a honeycake. Pellam counts out three coins. "Courier's pay. I'll log it as tea."

interaction_box_slide.narration: The caravan is almost here when the ground shrugs. The wardens' tall stacks of boxes start sliding down the bend. Both sides yelp. Time your dash.

interaction.cue: Dash across when the sliding boxes pause.

onSuccess.narration: You dart through the gap. The last stack thuds against a rock, and the top box bursts open. Something inside clicks.

onFailure.narration: A box bumps you into the heather, unhurt. The last stack thuds against a rock, and the top box bursts open. Something inside clicks.

onAssisted.narration: A warden and a mask haul you clear together. The top box bursts open. Something inside clicks.

scene_box_crawlers.narration: Out of the box tumble two bone crawlers: little scuttlers in borrowed bone, no bigger than footstools, all elbows. Their noses point down the hill. They smell the big stone's hum, and they want it for a snack. If they reach it, nobody will hold anything still.

encounter_crawlers.narration: The crawlers clatter down the bend, noses up, straight for the humming wagon. Turn them around before they reach it.

scene_crawlers_scattered.narration: The crawlers clatter off, elbows in the air. In the burst box lies a pebble that glints like a wink. "My lucky stone!" cries a warden. "Nine weeks I've looked for that!" She presses it into your hand. "Take it. I'll stop losing things." The first wagon comes around the corner.

scene_crawlers_boxed.narration: The crawlers swirl until the bend is all clatter. Then a mask drops a sack over one, and a warden slams the box lid. They sit on it together, arguing about who sat first. Something small and glinting rolls away downhill. The first wagon comes around the corner.

interaction_quiet_council.narration: You point to NOBODY SHOUTS. Pellam calls Hessa over to ask her straight. Each hero can offer a question, a worry or a hope. Hessa puts her ladle down so she can listen properly.

interaction_open_table.narration: You wave Hessa over and point to FACES SHOWING. Hessa lifts her mask. A helper from each camp sits down, and they agree to stand beside you tomorrow.

interaction_shared_soup.narration: You wave Hessa over and point to BRING ONE THING TO SHARE. Hessa brings soup. Pellam brings mugs. They serve each other and stay to talk. Tomorrow they will help brace the wagon together.

interaction_small_hum.narration: A passing warden takes the cart. You hold a little humming stone on a quiet rock. Wait for the calm middle of its pulse. A goat watches, chewing.

interaction.cue: Tap at the calm middle of the hum.

onSuccess.narration: For half a breath the hum rests. Remember that feeling for the wagon.

onFailure.narration: The hum slips away. The cart still gets home, and your other tools can help tomorrow.

onAssisted.narration: A singer hums under your note until it settles. Now you know the feeling.

interaction_practiced_hold.narration: You find the calm place inside the wagon's hum. It is bigger than the practice stone, with the same pulse. The mules wait, earmuffs half off.

interaction.cue: Tap at the calm middle, just as you practiced.

onSuccess.narration: The hum rests for one long breath. You let it go gently.

onFailure.narration: The pulse slips past your hands. The masks take the wagon.

onAssisted.narration: A singer helps you find the calm place. The hum rests, then returns gently.

interaction_ledger_limits.narration: The ledger says how to hold a hum: listen first, hold for one breath, then let go. Pellam underlined RELEASE so hard the next page has a dent.

interaction.cue: Set the safe limits in order: listen, hold, release.
clues: Release comes last. A tether must be able to let go.

onSuccess.narration: One breath of quiet, then a gentle release.

onFailure.narration: The steps tangle and the hum breaks free. The masks take the wagon.

onAssisted.narration: Pellam reads the steps while you work. The hum rests for one breath.

interaction_chord_hold.narration: Hessa sounds the notes: middle, low, high, middle. Echo them toward the wagon, so the stone has a note to rest on. One mule hums along, badly.

interaction.cue: Echo middle, low, high, middle after the notes glow.

onSuccess.narration: Your chord meets the stone's note. For one breath, the hillside is quiet.

onFailure.narration: The chord wobbles and the hum escapes. The masks take the wagon.

onAssisted.narration: The choir sings under your notes. The hum settles for one breath.

interaction_tether_team.narration: A warden blocks the wheel. A singer steadies the side. Brace together while you quiet the stone.

interaction.cue: Brace together while the stone is held for one breath.

onSuccess.narration: The wagon stands steady. You hold the hum for one breath, then let it go.

onFailure.narration: The helpers set another wheel block. Together you finish the test.

onAssisted.narration: Both helpers brace with you. The hum rests for one breath.

scene_helpers_brace.narration: The warden and the singer step up beside the wagon. One brings a wheel block. The other brings a steady note. They wait for your signal.

scene_visitors_brace.narration: Pellam and Hessa keep their promise. They bring a helper from each camp and show where to brace the wagon. Pellam logs the wheel block as SHARED.

interaction_quiet_council_response_quest.narration: Pellam needs safe limits. Hessa needs somebody to hear the choir. They answer each other, quietly. Tomorrow you can ask them to brace the wagon together.

interaction_quiet_council_response_worry.narration: Hessa agrees that a held note must also be allowed to stop. They answer each other, quietly. Tomorrow you can ask them to brace the wagon together.

interaction_quiet_council_response_hope.narration: Pellam asks Hessa to stand beside him at tomorrow's test. They answer each other, quietly. Tomorrow you can ask them to brace the wagon together.

voiceGuide.tone: warm, clever, a little spooky but never scary; two rival groups and the party as the table between them
forbidden: saying what is under the mountain

npcVoices.hessa: Deep Hollow choir member who ran the soup tent; gentle, wary, wants to trust you
npcVoices.old_ossley: very few words, long pauses that are not hesitation, answers the question you meant
npcVoices.mosshome_runner: breathless, cheerful, counts knots out loud
npcVoices.boggart: talks sidelong to nobody, never meets your eye, treasures overheard sentences
npcVoices.ford_witch: Mother Thrum, the ford witch; pointed hat, dry, kind underneath; only asks one question and means it
npcVoices.stall_witch: patched hat, brisk, charms ringing around her; lends questions, never sells them
npcVoices.centaur_relay: brisk, proud of the roads, delighted to be asked where something should go
npcVoices.exchange_merchant: Madame Coralie Fenn, the Exchange gem-buyer in a barrel on wheels; delighted to see you, genuinely fond, calls everyone darlings, and still a merchant
npcVoices.caravan_master: exhausted, practical, has had a headache since the stone came aboard
npcVoices.pellam: Pellam, warden ledger clerk; writes everything down twice, never smiles on duty, says no politely and means it; secretly fair
npcVoices.linnet: Cadet Linnet, a young warden scout; keen, stiff, trying to look older, softens fast
npcVoices.rook: Rook, a young mask scout from the choir; prickly, quick, curious under it

interaction_tea_cups.narration: As the sun goes down, Pellam waves a stack of tin mugs at you from the warden fires. "Tea for the other side," he says, as if it were an ordinary sentence. "From us. Hand to hand, please. Nobody has to cross anything." Far off across the dark strip of road, Hessa is holding out her empty hands.

interaction.cue: Catch the mug, then pass it along.

onSuccess.narration: Not a drop spills. At the far end Hessa takes the last mug, sniffs it, and sends a warm honeycake back down the line. Pellam counts three coins out of the camp's tea fund. "Courier's pay," he says. "I will log it as tea."

onFailure.narration: One mug slips, and a warden catches it with his boot. "Hot boot," he says, bravely. Everyone laughs, on both sides of the road, at the same time, and the rest of the tea goes through.

onAssisted.narration: Together you pass the mugs in a slow, steady row. Hessa takes the last one and sends a warm honeycake back down the line. Pellam counts three coins out of the tea fund. "Courier's pay," he says.

interaction_shared_soup.narration: You point at BRING ONE THING TO SHARE. Hessa brings soup. Pellam brings mugs, including one marked NOT SOUP. Pass a serving across without making anybody leave the table.

interaction.cue: Catch the serving, then pass it across the table.

onSuccess.narration: They stay to talk. Tomorrow they will help brace the wagon together. Pellam turns his mug around.

onFailure.narration: The visitors share what remains and stay to talk.

onAssisted.narration: Together you pass the soup across. Both visitors agree to help at the bend.

interaction_open_table.narration: You point at FACES SHOWING. Hessa lifts her mask. Pellam moves his ledger. Hold the wobbly door steady while they make room for a helper from each camp. Hessa has freckles. Pellam has soup on his sleeve.

interaction.cue: Steady the table while a warden and a singer make room.

onSuccess.narration: A warden and a singer agree to stand beside you tomorrow. The table has done its job.

onFailure.narration: The visitors steady the door and welcome a helper from each camp.

onAssisted.narration: Pellam props the short corner. Both camps promise a helper.

interaction_quiet_council.narration: You point to NOBODY SHOUTS. Pellam invites Hessa over to ask her directly. Each hero can offer a question, a worry or a hope. Hessa puts her ladle down so she can listen properly.

interaction.cue: Add a question, worry or hope before the visitors answer.

options.label: Ask what each side needs
options.reaction: Pellam needs safe limits. Hessa needs somebody to hear the choir.

options.label: Name a worry about control
options.reaction: Hessa agrees that a held note must also be allowed to stop.

options.label: Share a hope for working together
options.reaction: Pellam asks Hessa to stand beside him at tomorrow's test.

onSuccess.narration: They answer each other, quietly. Tomorrow you can ask them to brace the wagon together.

onFailure.narration: They keep talking with you between them.

onAssisted.narration: You take turns asking; the visitors listen and agree to help together.
